transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Ava Johnson, Maya Li, Tom Reyes, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair + open all-hands attendance (engineers, product, sales, ops, security)

00:00 Ava Johnson (CEO): ok good afternoon everybody, thanks for making time for a, uh, slightly condensed mid-year update. we'll run 60, maybe 75 minutes, Q&A at the end. quick landings: hiring, capacity, roadmap, and risk.
00:28 Maya Li (CTO): thanks Ava. i'll start on capacity — we have three levers: autoscale, Dedicated pool resizing, and smarter routing. we've seen tail latencies pop in north american regions when a single heavy customer spikes kv-cache warmups — or what the transcripts keep calling K V cash — aspects of cache warming are still noisy.
00:59 Tom Reyes (VP Eng): yeah and to add, the recent beta for continous batching hit some edge cases, some microbatched workloads actually increased p99 due to head-of-line blocking. that was unexpected. working on changing batching windows and adding adaptive timers.
01:30 Audience question (Xiao - Eng): can you clarify Dedicated vs Hosted for price sensitive customers?
01:36 Liam O'Connor (Head Product): short answer — Dedicated is for predictable high throughput and isolation; Hosted better for frictionless start. but important note: routing policies let you mix — we can route low-cost requests to quantized variants and high quality to full fp variants.
02:05 Maya Li: the Optimize team has a set of recommended quant profiles — new experiments show 4-bit q tokens with calibration keep quality loss below 1.5% for many retrieval tasks. caveat: not all seq lengths behave the same.
02:46 Priya Nair (Head People): on hiring — we are on track for 18 hires in Q3, focus on infra, SRE, and customer reliability engineers. interview loop changes rolling out next week. please escalate any concerns about capacity in hiring pipeline.
03:12 Ava: quick commercial note — renewal cadence is stable but we need to tighten our pilot-to-paid conversion. Sam from growth will share a cohort analysis.
03:29 Tom: on the private deployment front, security team finished SOC 2 readiness checklist and we have an internal audit scheduled for 2026-07-22. there were a few gaps in key rotation automation (KMS flows) that we need to close.
03:58 Audience murmur / small applause
04:10 Maya: moving into risk scenarios — scenario one: a heavy enterprise customer migrates to Private on-prem and we underprovision Dedicated pool for their canary, resulting in latency spikes for other hosted customers. mitigation: isolate that customer's traffic, run traffic shaping, and have automatic fallback to reduced QoS model variant.
04:45 Tom: scenario two: sudden GPU price increase on cloud provider. we have negotiated a short-term capacity buffer but we need a longer-term plan: multi-cloud redundancy and hedging with reserved capacity.
05:12 Liam: product roadmap — Q3 priorities include streaming improvements (chunked responses with better reconnect semantics), expanded function-calling surface, and the first public release of Optimize suggestions in console. i want to call out the 'reranker-as-a-service' pilot — shipping early beta for a retail customer.
05:43 Audience: question about latency vs cost tradeoffs, crowd noise.
06:00 Ava: ok we ran a quick poll earlier, 64% of respondents said cost is the primary blocker for wider adoption inside their teams. so we will prioritize at least two cost-saving features in next 90 days.
06:22 Maya: technical ask — we need everyone to run the new perf harness before 2026-07-07. it's in the infra repo, link in #infra. some folks had trouble with the new CUDA kernels, please open tickets.
07:05 Audience comment (security): are we supporting new compliance for EU data residency?
07:12 Tom: yes we are expanding region footprint, and private control plane options will let customers pin storage to a region. still working on audit log retention defaults.
07:38 Maya (muttering): also note that some product names get mangled in transcripts — Redwood Dedica — Dedicated — yes.
08:02 Q&A rapid fire — several questions about SSO / SAML integration. Liam: scheduled security workshop 2026-07-08 for vendor teams to cover SSO, SCIM and RBAC.
09:10 Audience (Engineer): any plans to open-source parts of the inference runtime?
09:15 Maya: we will open-source selected runtime optimizations but not the full kernel set. goal is community trust without giving away core IP.
09:38 Ava: culture update: people survey shows slower onboarding velocity and some confusion with IC leveling. Priya is leading a review to streamline onboarding by August.
10:05 Priya: we will publish a shortened onboarding checklist and pair new hires with a buddy. also reworking the 30/60/90 template.
10:32 Tom: ops update — new incident playbook live next week, includes automatic fallback to low-cost model variants and an early warning signal if token throughput jumps 20% over baseline in 5m windows.
10:55 Audience (Product): will rollback policies be automated?
11:01 Liam: yes, initial canary is manual, but the plan is automated rollback when quality deltas exceed configured thresholds; rollout schedule will be in product doc.
11:30 Ava: financial note — CFO shared updated burn runway model; two levers we can exercise: aggressive quantization + routing vs slower hiring. we prefer balanced approach; we cannot defer all hiring; long-term roadmap depends on both velocity and reliability.
12:05 Audience chatter — multiple people asking about bench results.
12:25 Tom: benchmark overview — early Dedicated bench shows linear scaling to 32 concurrent streams with our current kernel set, but p99 degrades at high sequence lengths; logs will be published.
12:58 Maya: ask for help — we need more test prompts for regression alerts. please submit prompt sets to the evals repo.
13:22 Audience applause; some cross talk.
13:40 Open Q&A circa 25 minutes — mixed questions about contract terms for Private, SLA commitments, and on-prem packaging.
14:10 Security rep (Jules): auditors requested full key rotation logs for last 12 months; we have partial coverage. action: security to run a gap remediation plan.
14:35 Priya: new parental leave policy rollout brief — effective 2026-08-01.
14:55 Ava: quick retrospective — what are one or two things to change?
15:05 Audience responses: improve internal doc discoverability; more transparent rollout notes; clearer call to action on bench participation.
15:40 Ava: ok closing — thanks for the candor. next all-hands will be an ops-heavy deep dive. closing notes: check #announcements for links to slides, bench spreadsheets, and SOC2 checklist.
15:58 Meeting end.

References / shared links mentioned (not included): slides deck (link in #announcements), perf harness repo (infra/perf-harness), capacity sensitivity sheet (to be posted by Maya), SOC2 readiness checklist (security docs).

Notes about transcript quality: occasional transcription errors (e.g., K V cash for KV cache, Redwood Dedicared, continous vs continuous, some proper names garbled).
